title: Agent Session Tracing: Native Trace Model vs Custom Logging

steps.prompt: Support engineers must work out why an Agentforce agent chose the wrong action in a given session: they need the reasoning steps, each action's inputs and outputs, and token usage per LLM call. Data 360 is provisioned in the org. Where should the engineers get this data?

options.label: Query the Session Tracing Data Model, joining steps to gateway request records
options.rationale: Session Tracing stores each session in standard Data 360 objects as a hierarchy of interactions and steps, including the planner's reasoning and each function call. Token and model details sit on the LLM-call records those steps reference, so one join answers all three needs without a parallel telemetry system.

options.label: Enable Apex debug logs at FINEST level for the agent's running user
options.rationale: Debug logs show the Apex that actions run, not the reasoning engine's planning between actions or the token usage of each LLM call.

options.label: Stream Real-Time Event Monitoring API events for the calls the agent's actions make
options.rationale: API events record which calls ran and who made them, but not the reasoning steps that chose the action or the tokens each LLM call used.

options.label: Have each action write its inputs and outputs to a custom log object
options.rationale: Action-level logs miss the reasoning steps between actions and rebuild telemetry that Session Tracing already captures as interaction steps.
